parastatals.name: Greater Bengaluru Authority and its city corporations
parastatals.notes: EVIDENCE: All points below come from the India Code full-text PDF of the GBA Act. This is the consolidated amended text, not a metadata-only page. Era=GBA-era. (1) Act and commencement: s.1(3), footnote 'came into force w.e.f. 15.05.2025' by Notification No. UDD 100 BBS 2025 P-2 dated 14.05.2025. The Act was first published in Karnataka Gazette Extra-ordinary No.240, Part IV-A, dated 24.04.2025. (2) Restructuring: s.7(1) says the Governor 'may' by notification constitute new City Corporations from BBMP areas. Under s.7(4), once the final notification is issued, BBMP 'shall cease to exist' and its assets and liabilities vest in the Government. s.5(1) caps the number of City Corporations at seven. Under s.26(5), corporation names carry the prefix 'Bengaluru' (e.g. 'Bengaluru South City Corporation'). s.361(1) repeals the BBMP Act, 2020 (Karnataka Act 53 of 2020) and the Rules made under it. (3) Body: s.9(1) says the Government 'shall' by notification constitute the Greater Bengaluru Authority within 120 days of commencement. Under s.9(2) it is a body corporate. Under s.9(3)(a) the Chief Minister is ex-officio Chairperson. (4) Chief executive: s.10(1) has the State appoint an officer not below the rank of Principal Secretary as Chief Commissioner. Under s.10(3) the Chief Commissioner 'shall be the Principal Executive Officer' of the GBA. For each City Corporation, s.84 provides for a Commissioner appointed by the Government, and s.85(1) says the Commissioner 'shall be the Chief Executive Officer of the Corporation'. (5) Budget: s.21 says the GBA 'shall prepare, every year … an annual budget estimate' and submit it to the Government. s.22(2) requires the Annual Report and Budget to be sent to the City Corporations. For City Corporations, s.182 has the Standing Committee for taxation, finance and appeals prepare a budget estimate, and s.182(2)(d) has the Commissioner print it and send it to Councillors by 1 February. has_annual_budget is null because these are legal duties only: no published GBA or City Corporation budget document was fetched, so actual publication is not proven. (6) Transition context: I saw a draft notification No. UDD 170 BBS 2025(e) dated 19.07.2025 (Karnataka Gazette Part III No. 403) under s.5(1)/s.7(1), proposing 5 City Corporations (Central, South, East, West, North). I saw it only through an aggregator (OpenCity), so it is a LEAD, not evidence, and is not cited. The final notification was not seen. | PLANNING BODIES (location notes only; all section numbers are from the GBA Act unless stated): (a) Greater Bengaluru Authority. s.14(2)(a): 'shall be the Planning Authority' as defined under the Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961, for the Greater Bengaluru Area. s.14(2)(b): may approve layouts in conformity with the master plan, while plan sanction for industrial units is done by the respective City Corporation. s.14(2)(d): development regulations apply uniformly across the area. s.15(1): responsible for master plan and mobility plans. s.11(3): Chief Town Planner of the rank of Director of Town and Country Planning, deputed by the Government. s.14(3)-(4): coordinates and supervises public authorities, with binding directions. s.19 gives the power to call for reports and issue directions to 'The Government' (wording recorded exactly). (b) City Corporations, GBA Act. s.107(2): Additional Chief Town Planner deputed from the Department of Town and Country Planning. s.14(2)(b): plan sanction for industrial units. (c) Bengaluru Metropolitan Planning Committee (BMPC). s.14(2)(c) says the State Government 'shall constitute' the BMPC under Article 243ZE, chaired by the Chief Minister, with the GBA Chief Commissioner as Member Secretary. The same clause also says 'The Bengaluru Metropolitan Planning Authority shall prepare a draft development plan' (the naming inconsistency is recorded exactly). s.103(1)(b): Ward Development Plans follow BMPC plans. Whether the BMPC has actually been constituted is not verified. (d) Bangalore Development Authority. Its Act (Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976) was not fetched [unverified]. It is named a 'public authority' in s.2(54). Its Commissioner sits on the GBA (s.9(3)(g)) and the Executive Committee (s.13(1)(d)). It is subject to GBA supervision under s.14(4). Its remaining planning role, if any, is not verified. (e) Bangalore Metropolitan Region Development Authority. Its Act (BMRDA Act, 1985) was not fetched [unverified]. Its Metropolitan Commissioner sits on the GBA (s.9(3)(u)) and the Executive Committee (s.13(1)(e)). (f) Department/Directorate of Town and Country Planning, under the Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961. That Act's text was not fetched [unverified]. The department supplies planners under s.11(3) and s.107(2). (g) KIADB. Under the s.14(2)(b) proviso it may sanction industrial layout and building plans in KIADB areas, in conformity with the master plan and with prior approval of the Local Planning Authority. Its Act was not fetched. (h) Directorate of Urban Land Transport (s.13(1)(f)) and Bengaluru Metropolitan Land Transport Authority (s.2(54)). Their Acts and instruments were not fetched. | DOMAINS: Candidate: bbmp.gov.in (gov.in domain). A web_search result for http://www.bbmp.gov.in/ was titled 'GBA - Greater Bengaluru Authority'. Its snippet showed GBA branding, the 1533 helpline and comm@bbmp.gov.in. However, when I fetched the same URL, it returned stale BBMP-era content (property tax and 2015 electoral roll notices), so it is not verified as currently showing GBA content. A Wikipedia infobox (blocked; lead only) gives 'gba.karnataka.gov.in' as the website. No tool returned that as a URL, so it is NOT listed. The X account @GBA_office links to bbmp.gov.in; this is social media, a lead only and not a website candidate. I tried fetching the Karnataka state portal department page (https://karnataka.gov.in/department/en) but it failed with url_not_allowed. After that the tool-use limit was exhausted, so no Urban Development Department or state-portal page linking to the GBA could be fetched. There is no government-page proof yet of which domain the government itself links to. | CONFIRM: (1) The date of the notification constituting the GBA under s.9(1). The team notes give 15 May 2025 and 2 Sept 2025. The official text confirms only that the Act commenced on 15.05.2025, so the GBA constitution date needs team confirmation. (2) The number, final-notification date and names of the City Corporations: only a draft notification of 19.07.2025 was seen, via an aggregator. (3) The official website: check whether gba.karnataka.gov.in exists and is linked from urbandevelopment/karnataka.gov.in, versus bbmp.gov.in. (4) Whether an Administrator (s.~ Administrator provisions) currently runs the City Corporations: a search snippet, unverified, mentions 'Chief Commissioner - GBA and Administrator - all Bengaluru City Corporations'. (5) Whether GBA and City Corporation budgets are published. (6) Whether the BMPC has been constituted, and what planning role remains with the BDA, BMRDA or the Directorate of Town and Country Planning. Check the KTCP Act 1961, BDA Act 1976 and BMRDA Act 1985 for amendments that substitute GBA for BBMP or BDA. (7) Amendments after Act 01 of 2026. I read the Second Amendment Bill (LA Bill No. 81 of 2025, a PRS copy, secondary); its contents match the Act 01 of 2026 changes shown in the India Code text. EVIDENCE: (all from the India Code PDF of the Act; era=GBA-era; the PDF has readable text and a header saying 'As amended by Acts 60 of 2025 and 01 of 2026', with assent dated 23 April 2025) Governing Act: s.1(3) and its footnote give the commencement date as 15.05.2025, per Notification No. UDD 100 BBS 2025 P-2 dated 14.05.2025. This official footnote settles the commencement date. The 2 Sept 2025 date appears only in blocked sources (Wikipedia), which tie it to the City Corporations' final notification; it is NOT verified. Structure: s.4 lists the civic authorities (GBA, City Corporations, Ward Committees). s.5(1) says the Governor 'shall' establish City Corporations, with a proviso capping them at 'not exceed seven'; the Statement of Objects and Reasons says 'not more than ten', which conflicts with the operative s.5. s.7 covers reconstitution of BBMP: draft notification, final notification, and BBMP 'shall cease to exist' (s.7(4)). s.8(3): GBA 'shall discharge the role of coordinator' (substituted by Act 60 of 2025 w.e.f. 12.09.2025). s.9: GBA is a body corporate with the Chief Minister as ex-officio Chairperson. s.361(1) repeals the BBMP Act, 2020 and its Rules. Chief executive: s.10(1),(3) say the State Government 'shall appoint' a Chief Commissioner (not below Principal Secretary rank), who 'shall be the Principal Executive Officer' of GBA. s.25 lists the Commissioner as an authority of each City Corporation. s.84 says the Commissioner is appointed by the Government (not below Secretary rank). s.85(1) says the Commissioner 'shall be the Chief Executive Officer of the Corporation'. So has_chief_executive=true; the post exists in law. Budget: s.21 says GBA 'shall prepare, every year' an annual budget estimate and submit it to the Government. s.22(2) says GBA shall give its Annual Report and Budget to the City Corporations. s.181(5) says the City Corporation Commissioner 'shall prepare a budget estimate', and s.181(7) requires it to be prepared, presented and adopted as prescribed. These are legal duties only. I fetched no official published GBA or City Corporation budget, so has_annual_budget=null: a legal provision is not proof that budgets are published. | PLANNING BODIES: (location notes only, no verdicts) (1) Greater Bengaluru Authority: GBG Act 2024 s.14(2)(a) says 'Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law', GBA 'shall be the Planning Authority' under the Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961 for the Greater Bengaluru Area. Under s.14(2)(b), layout approval 'may be done by' GBA and industrial plan sanction goes to the respective City Corporation. Under s.14(2)(d), development regulations apply uniformly. s.14(3) covers schemes and binding directions; s.14(4) covers coordination and supervision of BDA, BWSSB, BMTC, BSWML, BMRCL, BESCOM and similar bodies, with binding directions (substituted by Act 60 of 2025 w.e.f. 12.09.2025). s.19 is a power of supervision and directions (heading only; not read in full). (2) Bengaluru Metropolitan Planning Committee (BMPC): under s.14(2)(c) the State Government 'shall constitute' it per Article 243ZE, chaired by the CM, with the GBA Chief Commissioner as Member Secretary. The same clause then says the 'Bengaluru Metropolitan Planning Authority shall prepare a draft development plan'; this wording is recorded exactly. Whether the BMPC has been constituted is NOT verified. (3) KIADB: under the s.14(2)(b) proviso it may sanction industrial layout and building plans in KIADB areas, in conformity with the master plan and with prior approval of the 'concerned Local Planning Authority'. KIADB's own Act was not read. (4) City Corporations: s.223 requires them to act in conformity with the KTCP Act 1961 and the Master Plan, or with the Planning Authority's concurrence. s.224 says building bye-laws are made with GBA approval, based on GBA model bye-laws. Schedule I (s.111) lists 'Urban planning including town planning' as a core function. (5) Bangalore Development Authority: it appears in the Act only as a GBA ex-officio member (s.9(3)(g), its Commissioner) and as a body GBA supervises (s.14(4)). The BDA Act, 1976 and any change to BDA's planning-authority status were NOT read [unverified]. (6) BMRDA and the state Town Planning Department: not named in the passages read; their Acts and roles were NOT verified. (7) The KTCP Act 1961 itself was not fetched [unverified]. | DOMAINS: (1) https://www.gba.karnataka.gov.in/ was returned by web_search with the title 'GBA - Greater Bengaluru Authority'. It is a karnataka.gov.in subdomain, which is a strong signal. However, web_fetch refused it (url_not_allowed), so I could not read the page, and I fetched no state portal or UDD page that links to it. Its official status rests on the domain only. (2) http://www.bbmp.gov.in/ is the legacy BBMP domain. web_search listed it with the title 'GBA - Greater Bengaluru Authority', and the search snippet showed the GBA Chief Commissioner with the email comm@bbmp.gov.in (snippet only, not proof). My web_fetch returned stale BBMP-era content (2015 electoral roll and similar items), so it does not currently prove a GBA identity. No separate official websites for the individual City Corporations were found from any tool; their X accounts and Wikipedia pages are excluded. | CONFIRM: (a) I could not fetch any official state portal or Urban Development Department page linking to the GBA website: the search tool limit was reached, and the gba.karnataka.gov.in fetch was refused. A human should open https://www.gba.karnataka.gov.in/ and a UDD or karnataka.gov.in page that links to it. (b) The GBA constitution notification under s.9(1) and its date. (c) The final notification establishing the City Corporations under ss.5 and 7(3). Blocked leads (Wikipedia, news, opencity) suggest five corporations (Central, North, South, East and West) and a final notification dated 2 Sept 2025 in Karnataka Gazette Extraordinary No. 522; the draft is said to be UDD 170 BBS 2025(e) of 19 July 2025. All of this is unverified; the official Karnataka eGazette copy is needed. (d) Whether GBA and the City Corporations have actually published budgets for 2025-26 and 2026-27; a blocked lead suggests a Bengaluru West City Corporation budget for 2026-27. (e) The status of BDA and BMRDA as planning bodies after GBG Act s.14(2)(a), and whether the BMPC has been constituted. (f) The research-team note matches the source on the Act replacing BBMP. Of the two candidate dates, only 15.05.2025 (commencement of the Act) is confirmed by an official source. EVIDENCE: Every legal point below comes from the full text of Karnataka Act 36 of 2025 on India Code (indiacode.nic.in PDF). This is the actual text with amendment footnotes, not a metadata page. Era = GBA-era. (1) Act and name: s.1(1) gives the short title 'Greater Bengaluru Governance Act, 2024'. s.1(3) footnote gives commencement w.e.f. 15.05.2025 (Notification No. UDD 100 BBS 2025 P-2 dated 14.05.2025). This confirms the team's 15 May 2025 date as the Act's commencement only. s.4 names the Civic Authorities: the Greater Bengaluru Authority, the City Corporations and the Ward Committees. s.5 lets the Governor establish City Corporations, with a proviso that there shall be no more than seven. s.7 'Reconstitution of Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike': a draft notification, then a final notification under s.7(3), after which s.7(4) says BBMP 'shall cease to exist'. s.9(1): the Government shall constitute the GBA by notification within 120 days of commencement; s.9(2) makes it a body corporate. s.361(1) repeals the BBMP Act, 2020. (2) Chief executive: s.10(3) says the Chief Commissioner 'shall be the Principal Executive Officer' of the GBA. s.84 says the Commissioner of each City Corporation is appointed by the Government. s.85(1) says the Commissioner 'shall be the Chief Executive Officer of the Corporation'. These are posts created by law. A search snippet of bbmp.gov.in names a Chief Commissioner - GBA who is also Administrator of all city corporations. That is a snippet only: not verified, and not used as evidence. (3) Budget: s.21 says the GBA 'shall prepare, every year' an annual budget estimate and submit it to the Government. s.22(2) says the GBA's annual report and budget are copied to the City Corporations. For each City Corporation, s.181 covers preparing the budget, s.182 says the Standing Committee for taxation, finance and appeals prepares the estimate, and s.184 says the Corporation 'shall finally pass the budget estimate' at least three weeks before the year starts. has_annual_budget is left null: the law requires a budget, but I did not fetch any published GBA or corporation budget, and a legal provision does not prove practice. | PLANNING BODIES: (a) GBA, under the Greater Bengaluru Governance Act, 2024. s.14(2)(a) makes it the 'Planning Authority' under the Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961 for the Greater Bengaluru Area. s.14(2)(b) says layout approval 'may be done by' the GBA, and industrial-unit plan sanction is done by the City Corporation. s.15 covers the master plan and major projects. s.14(3)-(4) give coordination and binding-direction powers over public authorities. s.19 is the power of supervision and directions (seen in the contents list only). (b) Bengaluru Metropolitan Planning Committee (BMPC). Under s.14(2)(c) the State 'shall constitute' it under Article 243ZE, chaired by the Chief Minister, with the GBA Chief Commissioner as Member Secretary. The same clause says the 'Bengaluru Metropolitan Planning Authority shall prepare a draft development plan'. That wording is recorded exactly as written; whether the BMPC has actually been constituted is not verified. (c) City Corporations, under the same Act. Building bye-laws are made 'With the approval of the Greater Bengaluru Authority' (s.224). Land-use matters need the Master Plan or the concurrence of the Planning Authority under the KTCP Act, 1961 (the provision just before s.224). (d) Bangalore Development Authority. Its Commissioner is an ex-officio GBA member (s.9(3)(g)), and s.14(4) lists BDA among the bodies the GBA supervises. BDA's own Act (Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976) is [unverified]: not fetched. (e) Bengaluru Metropolitan Region Development Authority. Its Metropolitan Commissioner is an ex-officio GBA member (s.9(3)(u)). Its Act (BMRDA Act, 1985) is [unverified]: not fetched. (f) KIADB, under the s.14(2)(b) proviso: it may sanction plans in KIADB industrial areas in line with the master plan and with prior approval of the Local Planning Authority. Its Act was not fetched. (g) State town planning department. Its role was not researched; the KTCP Act, 1961 text was not fetched. | DOMAINS: Candidate 1 is gba.karnataka.gov.in, a subdomain of the Karnataka state portal domain (gov.in). The search result was titled 'GBA - Greater Bengaluru Authority', but the fetch was refused by the tool (url_not_allowed), so the content was not verified. Candidate 2 is bbmp.gov.in, the old BBMP domain (gov.in). Its search snippet showed GBA branding, the email comm@bbmp.gov.in, the GBA Chief Commissioner, and links to the Urban Development Department, GoK and the Centre for e-Governance. However, my own fetch of http://www.bbmp.gov.in/ returned old BBMP content (2015 electoral roll, trade licence notices), so what the site currently shows is uncertain. I found no separate official websites for the individual City Corporations; only an X account came up, which is excluded. I could not fetch any Urban Development Department or state portal page linking to either domain because the tool-use limit ran out. So step 2 of the website check (a gov.in page linking to the site) was NOT done. | CONFIRM: (1) Fetch an official UDD or state portal page that links to gba.karnataka.gov.in, and check whether bbmp.gov.in now redirects there. (2) Find in the eGazette or on the UDD site: the notification constituting the GBA under s.9, and the final notification under s.7(3) constituting the City Corporations (number, names, date). Only after that, decide whether 2 Sept 2025 is the effective date; it is not verified, so for now it needs team confirmation. The amendment by Act 60 of 2025 is w.e.f. 12.09.2025, which is a different date. (3) Check whether any amendment after Act 01 of 2026 exists. (4) Check whether the GBA and corporation budgets are actually published, then set has_annual_budget. (5) Get official texts of the BDA Act 1976, BMRDA Act 1985 and KTCP Act 1961, and check how the GBA's role as planning authority sits alongside BDA's planning powers under those Acts. (6) Check whether the BMPC has been constituted, and why s.14(2)(c) refers to both the 'Committee' and a 'Bengaluru Metropolitan Planning Authority'. (7) Get the GBA's RTI 4(1)(b) disclosures and the officers' government email addresses. EVIDENCE: Governing Act. The India Code bitstream PDF (indiacode.nic.in, Government of India) contains the full readable text of Karnataka Act No. 36 of 2025, with amendment footnotes. S.1(3) has a footnote saying the Act came into force w.e.f. 15.05.2025 by Notification No. UDD 100 BBS 2025 P-2 dated 14.05.2025. This official footnote settles the commencement date. The other date (2 Sept 2025, said to be when the corporations were formed) appears only in blocked news and Wikipedia leads and is NOT verified. ; S.4: the civic authorities are (a) the Greater Bengaluru Authority, (b) the City Corporations and (c) the Ward Committees. ; S.5(1): the Governor 'shall' establish City Corporations; the proviso caps them at seven. ; S.7(1)-(4): new City Corporations are formed by notification, with a draft notification and 30 days for objections. On the final notification, 'the Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike ... shall cease to exist'. ; S.9(1): the Government 'shall, by notification' set up the GBA no later than 120 days after commencement. The GBA is a body corporate (s.9(2)), chaired ex officio by the Chief Minister. ; S.360: rules, notifications and orders under the Karnataka Municipal Corporations Act, 1976 and the BBMP Act, 2020 stay in force as long as they are not inconsistent with the new Act. S.361: the BBMP Act, 2020 (Karnataka Act 53 of 2020) and its Rules are repealed. ; Chief executive: S.10(1) says the State Government 'shall appoint' a Chief Commissioner not below Principal Secretary rank. S.10(3) makes the Chief Commissioner the 'Principal Executive Officer' of the GBA. S.25(b) and s.84 create a Commissioner for each City Corporation, appointed by the Government and not below Secretary rank. S.85(1) says the Commissioner 'shall be the Chief Executive Officer of the Corporation'. This shows the posts exist in law. I did not verify who holds them now. ; Annual budget: the law requires one but publication is not verified. S.21 says the GBA 'shall prepare, every year ... an annual budget estimate' and submit it to the Government. S.22 covers the annual report, which is laid before the Legislature and copied to the Corporations. For the City Corporations, s.181 says the Commissioner 'shall prepare a budget estimate', and s.182 covers the Standing Committee for taxation, finance and appeals. The 2026-27 GBA and corporation budgets appear only in blocked leads (OpenCity, news). I found no official published budget, so has_annual_budget=null. ; Wording: the Act's 'public authority' definition (s.2(54)) and its membership lists name 'Bangalore Development Authority', 'Bangalore Metropolitan Region Development Authority' and others. The Act does not use the phrase 'Corporation of the City of Bangalore'. | PLANNING BODIES (location only, no verdicts): (1) Greater Bengaluru Authority, under the GBG Act 2024. S.14(2)(a), which applies 'notwithstanding anything contained in any other law', makes the GBA the 'Planning Authority' under the Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961 for the Greater Bengaluru Area. S.14(2)(b) says layout approval 'may be done' by the GBA, plan sanction for industrial units is done by the respective City Corporation, and there is a KIADB proviso. S.14(2)(d) applies one set of land and building regulations across the whole area. S.14(3)-(4) and s.19 give coordination, binding-direction and supervision powers over public authorities, including BDA, BWSSB, BMTC, BSWML, BMRCL and BESCOM; s.19 was located from the arrangement of sections only. The Chief Town Planner of the GBA is a member (s.9(3)(q)). ; (2) Bengaluru Metropolitan Planning Committee (BMPC), under s.14(2)(c) of the GBG Act read with Article 243ZE of the Constitution. The State Government 'shall constitute' it; the Chief Minister chairs it and the GBA Chief Commissioner is Member Secretary. The same clause then says the 'Bengaluru Metropolitan Planning Authority shall prepare a draft development plan'; this wording is recorded exactly. Whether the BMPC has actually been constituted is not verified. ; (3) City Corporations, under the GBG Act. The section just before s.224 (number not seen) ties land-use permissions to the KTCP Act, 1961 and the Master Plan, or to the Planning Authority's concurrence where there is no Master Plan. S.224 says Corporations make building bye-laws with GBA approval, based on GBA model bye-laws. S.103(1)(b) has ward plans follow the BMPC plans. ; (4) Bangalore Development Authority, under the BDA Act, 1976 [Act text not fetched, unverified]. Its Commissioner is an ex officio member of the GBA (s.9(3)(g)) and of the Executive Committee (s.13), and the GBA supervises it under s.14(4). ; (5) Bangalore Metropolitan Region Development Authority, under the BMRDA Act, 1985 [Act text not fetched, unverified]. Its Metropolitan Commissioner sits on the GBA Executive Committee (s.13). ; (6) State Department of Town and Country Planning, under the KTCP Act, 1961 [not fetched]. The KTCP Act is the parent planning law cited in s.14(2)(a). | DOMAINS: Only one government-domain candidate came back from a tool: http://www.bbmp.gov.in/. Its search result was titled 'GBA - Greater Bengaluru Authority', but the fetched copy showed old BBMP homepage text with 2015-era items, so it may be stale or a legacy site. No gov.in or nic.in page linking to it was fetched, so it is NOT proven to be the current GBA site. The domain 'gba.karnataka.gov.in' appeared only as text inside a blocked Wikipedia snippet; no tool returned it as a URL, so it is not listed. No websites for the individual City Corporations were found from any tool; only X/Twitter accounts and Wikipedia came up, and those are not allowed. Step 2 (fetching state portal and Urban Development Department pages that link to the GBA) could NOT be done because the tool-use limit ran out during the run. | CONFIRM: (a) The official GBA website (check gba.karnataka.gov.in through a Karnataka UDD or state portal link) and whether bbmp.gov.in now redirects to it. (b) The gazette notification constituting the GBA under s.9, and its date. (c) The final notification under s.7(3) forming the City Corporations: how many there are (leads say five: Central, North, South, East, West), their names, and whether 2 Sept 2025 is the correct date. Until then, the date of the change from BBMP to GBA needs team confirmation. (d) The published 2026-27 GBA and corporation budgets on an official site. (e) Whether the BMPC has been constituted. (f) Amendments after 07.01.2026, and official texts of the BDA Act 1976, BMRDA Act 1985 and KTCP Act 1961, including how the BDA's planning role stands now that s.14(2)(a) makes the GBA the Planning Authority. parastatals.current_status: The Act is in force from 15.05.2025, according to the official text (era: GBA-era). The Act provides for a Greater Bengaluru Authority (s.9) and up to seven City Corporations (s.5). BBMP stops existing when the final notification under s.7(3) is issued, and the BBMP Act, 2020 is repealed (s.361). I did not see in any official source the notifications that actually set up the GBA and the City Corporations, or how many corporations there are or when they were created. Needs team confirmation.
